visible_observation: The headline 'WHERE THE HOUSES END' is set in a serif typeface with extreme letter-spacing (tracking), creating a wide, rigid bar of text that sits in a dark header block completely detached from the atmospheric imagery below.
critique: The excessive tracking reduces the title to a decorative graphic element rather than a readable headline, creating a 'wall of text' effect that feels cold and mechanical. By isolating the title in a separate header block, the design fails to integrate the text with the visual metaphor of the fading town, missing the opportunity to have the words physically interact with the environment.
revision: Reduce the letter-spacing of the headline to a standard or slightly wide setting to restore readability and warmth. Move the title out of the header block and overlay it directly onto the upper portion of the misty road, allowing the text to fade slightly into the background fog to visually reinforce the theme of disappearing places.
protected_strength: The atmospheric perspective of the road and the subtle, low-contrast color palette that establishes the melancholic, cinematic mood.
